info: Hardwood, highly durable and rot-resistant. Used for flooring and heavy construction.
Hardwood, incredibly common in Russia. Uniform texture, excellent for plywood and furniture.
Softwood, widely used in Russian construction. Easy to work with and resinous.
Softwood, highly valued in Russia for its extreme water resistance and durability.
Softwood, lightweight and resonant. Commonly used for general lumber and musical instruments.
Engineered wood composite made from wood fibers. Smooth surface, easy to machine and paint, used for furniture and doors.
MDF treated with special resins (often tinted green in core) for use in humid environments like bathrooms and kitchens.
Medium-density fiberboard coated with a decorative melamine film. Widely used for premium furniture facades.
Low-cost engineered wood made from wood chips and resin pressed together. Standard material for budget cabinetry.
Melamine-faced particleboard. The most common material for carcass furniture, kitchen cabinets, and wardrobes in Russia.
Particleboard made with moisture-resistant resins (usually has a green core). Used for kitchen countertops and bathroom vanities.
Sheet material manufactured from thin layers of rotary-cut wood veneer glued together with alternating grain direction.
Moisture-resistant plywood bonded with urea-formaldehyde glue. Safe for interior furniture, wall sheathing, and eco-friendly projects.
Highly water-resistant plywood bonded with phenol-formaldehyde glue. Toxic for indoor use, designed for outdoor construction and roofing.
FSF plywood coated with a protective plastic or resin film. Highly water-resistant, heavily used for concrete formwork and truck flooring.
Engineered wood particle board formed by adding adhesives and then compressing layers of wood strands in specific orientations.
Thin, dense sheet material often used for the back walls of cabinet furniture and drawer bottoms.
